details: U.S. spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced a significant net outflow of $1.28 billion in the week ending November 6, 2026. This marks their worst weekly performance since late June and has reversed their year-to-date gains, resulting in approximately $914.1 million in net outflows for 2026. BlackRock's IBIT fund alone registered $403 million in outflows on Friday. Additionally, spot Ether ETFs also faced substantial outflows, losing $365.3 million and extending their negative streak for the sixth consecutive week.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $1.28 Billion Outflow, Flip Negative for 2026

details: The total cryptocurrency market capitalization decreased by 7.32% to $2.58 trillion on November 6, 2026, with Bitcoin's price dropping below $76,000—a $4,197.53 decline from the previous day. This broad market downturn is largely attributed to a wider "risk-off" sentiment in financial markets, massive liquidations of approximately $1.08 billion in leveraged long positions, and a 5.52% plunge in the Nasdaq Composite, driven by concerns over stricter AI regulation and a sell-off in technology stocks.
title: Crypto Market Down 7.32% as Bitcoin Falls Below $76,000 Amid Nasdaq Plunge

details: The cryptocurrency market continues to exhibit weakness, with investor confidence remaining fragile due to recent macroeconomic and political developments. The U.S. midterm elections, which saw the Democratic Party secure control of both the Senate and the House, alongside a strong Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, have reinforced a bearish bias. Expectations of a more restrictive stance from the Federal Reserve following the NFP data suggest higher interest rates, which typically reduce market liquidity and diminish the appeal of risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: Political Uncertainty & NFP Data Weigh on Crypto Market Confidence

details: In contrast to the overall negative trend in the cryptocurrency market, the DeFi token Uniswap (UNI) recorded a 4% increase on November 7, 2026. This upward movement occurred while other altcoins, such as Cardano, experienced declines, and XRP reached a multi-week low. Uniswap's performance suggests a selective resilience within the decentralized finance (DeFi) sector despite the general market weakness.
title: Uniswap Rises 4% Amidst Broader Crypto Market Downturn

details: The total supply of stablecoins decreased by approximately $5 billion in the week ending November 7, 2026, representing a 1.7% reduction. This decline, with some trackers reporting even larger drops, indicates a withdrawal of capital from the broader crypto ecosystem. Despite this outflow, Ethereum (ETH) has shown relative stability, experiencing only a minor 1% drop over the past week. This divergence has led investors to question whether this calm period for ETH might precede a more significant market correction.
title: Stablecoin Supply Dips by $5 Billion in a Week, Raising Concerns for Ethereum
